newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek mutual fund assets up 3.5pct mo/mo in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Greek mutual fund assets up 3.5pct mo/mo in Sept.

text.p: Greece's mutual fund industry saw assets under management rise 3.55 percent month-on-month to 3.364 trillion drachmas at the end of September compared to 3.249 trillion on August 31, the Union of Greek Institutional Investors said in a statement.
The assets of fixed income funds rose 3.82 percent month-on-month in September, money market funds 10.82 percent, balanced funds by 9.35 percent and growth funds by 5.31 percent, it said.
Xios fixed income fund ranks first among funds of its class with a year-to-end September return of 13.1 percent.
The average return for all fixed income funds was 9.96 percent in the same period.
Triaina money market fund topped its class in terms of year-to-end September return with 11.79 percent. The average return of this class of funds was 8.76 percent.
ABN-AMRO led all growth funds with a year-to-end September return of 12.18 percent. The avearge return stood at 2.79 percent.
Delos balanced fund was ahead of all funds of its category with a return of 14.49 percent. The average return for balanced funds stood at 5.24 percent.

The Interamerican dollar money market fund was the top performer among all international money market funds with a return of 6.56 percent and Templeton growth was leading all international growth funds with 10.48 percent.
Delos international bonds fund ranked first with 8.92 percent among all world bond mutual funds. The year-to-end September rise was 38.15 percent or 929.1 billion drachmas.

Six new mutual funds started in September - Cretafund fixed income, Cretafund growth, Cretafund money market, Allianz short-term investments, Barclays domestic bonds and money markets, bringing the total number of Greek mutual funds to 138.
The three Cretafunds are administered by the Alpha mutual fund management company, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
